articles.title: La 'pesadilla' de De Ligt en su reestreno con el United... ¡326 días después!
articles.standfirst: El central del Manchester United volvió a la acción como titular ante el Como y se vio completamente superado
articles.summary: El central del Manchester United volvió a la acción como titular ante el Como y se vio completamente superado
articles.body: Corría el verano de 2019 cuando Matthijs de Ligt (Países Bajos, 1999) 'voló' de aquel Ajax que alcanzó las semifinales de la Champions como el central más caro de la historia (85.5 millones de euros) en aquel momento. Sin embargo, no terminó de 'cuajar' en Juventus, Bayern Múnich... ni tampoco Manchester United. Las lesiones han tenido gran parte de culpa de que el central que más millones ha movido (197.5) en materia de fichajes nunca haya llegado a ser lo que un día prometía cuando 'Tuttosport' le eligió como Golden Boy en 2018. La última le ha tenido fuera de los terrenos de juego... ¡durante 326! Desde aquella remontada contra el Crystal Palace en Selhurst Park en la que completó los 90', todavía con Rúben Amorim en el banquillo, De Ligt no se había vuelto a enfundar la elástica del Manchester United a causa de una lesión de espalda que, después de varios meses experimentando con un tratamiento conservador, le obligó a pasar por quirófano. "Desde noviembre, lo he dado todo. Me he esforzado al máximo en cada entrenamiento y explorando todas las opciones para volver a hacer lo que me apasiona: jugar al fútbol", reconoció el central neerlandés. "Agradezco a todos los que me han apoyado durante este difícil periodo de mi carrera. Sigo tan decidido como siempre a defender los colores del Manchester United y a jugar ante nuestra increíble afición lo antes posible". Empezó a reincorporarse a la dinámica del equipo durante las últimas semanas y, después de estar presente en el banquillo contra el Atlético de Madrid y el Leeds, Michael Carrick sorprendió alineándole como titular en el eje de la zaga junto a Harry Maguire por delante de Lisandro Martínez o Lenny Yoro. "Es fantástico tenerlo de vuelta. Ha recorrido un largo camino. Ha estado de baja alrededor de 11 meses en los que ha tenido que ser paciente y trabajar duro", exponía Michael Carrick en la previa del partido sobre el césped del Giuseppe Sinigaglia. "Está en forma y está listo. Lleva ya varias semanas entrenando, así que se encuentra en muy buena forma". La realidad, sin embargo, fue muy diferente. Y es que, al igual que todo el Manchester United, De Ligt se vio tremendamente superado: tan sólo realizó dos acciones defensivas, apenas recuperó dos balones, no disputó ni un duelo área, ganó uno de los dos que batalló por alto y tampoco realizó ninguna falta. No fue porque no tuviese trabajo... sino porque no llegaba a las acciones. Una circunstancia que quedó completamente patente en el 2-0 anotado por un Douvikas que, mientras le dibujaba el desmarque a Nico Paz, destrozó a De Ligt a base a amagos y cambios de dirección. Tampoco llegó a la cobertura en el 3-0 de Nico Paz y dimitió en el 4-0 anotado por Jacobo Ramón de cabeza en el área pequeña. Una 'pesadilla'. "Hemos alineado a De Ligt como titular cuando llevaba sin disputar ni un minuto desde el mes de noviembre de la pasada temporada. Obviamente, se notó", expuso Peter Schmeichel después del partido. Es quien menos cuota de responsabilidad debería tener... a pesar de salir señalado en numerosas acciones. Lo contrario hubiese sido sorprendente. Ahora bien, el hecho de que Carrick tuviese que reclutarlo vino a reflejar la desesperación que atraviesa un Manchester United que enlaza siete partidos sin ganar.

articles.title: A veces ir peor... es volver mejor
articles.standfirst: El Madrid suele sacar petróleo cuando el Barça llega al Clásico muy favorito: y el del domingo es el que más en 10 años (60,69%)
articles.summary: El Madrid suele sacar petróleo cuando el Barça llega al Clásico muy favorito: y el del domingo es el que más en 10 años (60,69%)
articles.body: El Barça tiene el mayor favoritismo en 10 años a ganar un Clásico (60,69%, ocho puntos por encima de lo habitual), pero a veces no es una noticia mala para el Real Madrid, porque en el balance histórico, siempre que el Barça fue muy, muy favorito... ganó el Madrid. Lo analiza en un largo informe Betfair, que tiene una poderosa base de datos de pronósticos y favoritos y además, análisis estadísticos que suelen usar los traders usando históricos, momentos de forma y otros muchos factores cruzados. El Barça aterriza invicto en Liga, que no en Champions, con su mayor favoritismo desde 2012, si bien los culés han sido favoritos en los últimos 15 clásicos disputados en su hogar, pero en esta serie sólo venció cinco: casi dos victorias por debajo de la expectativa acumulada. El Real Madrid, por el contrario, se crece en territorio culé con 1,31 triunfos más de la expectativa acumulada. Y cuanto menos favorito, más opciones de ganar. Y en el del domingo tiene apenas un 22,76%. En las dos ocasiones únicas ocasiones en las que el Real Madrid estuvo por debajo del 20% de opciones de triunfo acabó ganando: en 2012 y en 2016. En total, acumulaba una expectativa de 3,69 victorias en los últimos 15, pero terminó imponiéndose en cinco ocasiones. Los empates, por su parte, también superaron ligeramente las previsiones: se esperaban 3,50 y se produjeron cuatro. Queda demostrado que el tópico ‘En un Clásico todo puede pasar’ tiene algo de cierto. De los 15 Clásicos analizados, el Barcelona, pese a partir como favorito en todos ellos, solo consiguió la victoria en seis ocasiones (40%). Los otros nueve encuentros terminaron con cuatro empates y cinco triunfos del Real Madrid. De hecho, en ocho de esos 15 Clásicos el Barça superaba el 55% de probabilidades de victoria, más del doble de las opciones de su eterno rival. Sin embargo, solo logró imponerse en cuatro de ellos (50%), mientras que los otros cuatro se saldaron con dos empates y dos victorias madridistas.

articles.title: Hacia un Clásico con cartas nuevas
articles.standfirst: La opinión de Alfredo Relaño
articles.summary: La opinión de Alfredo Relaño
articles.body: Llega el Clásico (algunos ya dicen que la vida es lo que pasa entre un Clásico y el siguiente) y de repente las cosas ya no son como eran, porque el Barça viene de perder 4-2 y el Madrid de ganar 4-1. Por supuesto, las condiciones eran distintas: el Barça visitó al campeón de Europa, el Madrid recibió al séptimo de la Bundesliga. Pero aún así, la percepción en la calle ha cambiado. El Barça ha perdido por primera vez. Con paliativos reales, desde luego, desde el campo ajeno y la calidad del rival hasta la automutilación al dejar a Rodri fuera durante dos terceras partes del encuentro, pero perdió de forma contundente y con el portero como mejor jugador, lo que pone el foco sobre su depauperada defensa, que arrastra bajas. Y aunque marcó dos goles, el ataque no estuvo bien: Lamine hizo su primer partido pálido de la temporada, aunque se tapó con un golazo, Raphinha está recuperándose y Gordon no dio la talla. Para empeorar las cosas, Olmo se lesionó y estará ausente. En el boxeo se ha dado mucho el caso del boxeador invencible que de repente sufre un K.O., pierde, sufre la conciencia de invencibilidad y “aprende a caer”, según expresión hecha. No digo que este vaya a ser el caso del Barça, pero es una posibilidad que acaricia el madridista. Ya no teme más el partido. La otra baza es la evolución positiva del Madrid, con ese nuevo modelo que mezcla músculo y control en el medio campo (sean Tchoauméni-Güler o Camavinga-Bernardo Silva) y traslada a Valverde a la derecha. Eso más el emergente Diomande, que está mejorando a Vinicius en el extremo izquierda hasta el punto de que no es ningún secreto que para muchos madridistas la sanción al brasileño ha acabado por ser un bien. Que todo esto dé para que el Madrid gane es muy dudoso, pero dota al partido de una cierta intriga que hace un mes no hubiera tenido. Y falta saber si Mourinho perseverará en la nueva línea o blindará el equipo por lo que pueda pasar, ante el recuerdo de su primera experiencia como madridista en el Camp Nou

articles.title: Las notas de la semana: lo del United no tiene nombre
articles.standfirst: Por Juan Ignacio García-Ochoa
articles.summary: Por Juan Ignacio García-Ochoa
articles.body: El United sigue deambulando por Europa y regalando el presente. El Como le hizo cuatro y confirmó que el gigante inglés ya no intimida ni con el nombre. No es la peor nota de la semana, pero sí la más llamativa. El salto que le faltaba. Campeón del Masters 1000 de Shanghái después de remontar a Rafa Jódar una final española: 1-6, 7-6 y 6-4. El mayor título de su carrera merece el sobresaliente y le vale además ser el quinto hombre en la Davis. Liderado por un genial Isco, el Betis suma nueve puntos de nueve en la Champions. Datos históricos para un equipo que sueña con llegar muy lejos en esta Champions. No es de los favoritos, pero lo tiene todo: estrella, equipo, entrenador y una afición de 10. Debutar en la NBA y ponerle un tapón a Wembanyama es una buena manera de presentarse. Aday Mara aprovechó sus primeros minutos oficiales con los Thunder para sumar siete puntos, dos rebotes y una asistencia en la victoria ante San Antonio. Un primer paso que invita a seguir mirando al pívot con ilusión. Desde el día de su debut está jugando con el 130 de lo que ha costado en la espalda. Pero poco a poco está soltando la presión y está demostrando que independientemente del precio, es un jugador extraordinario. Sus dos últimos goles y su rendimiento en el último mes le convierten en una de las principales esperanzas del Madrid en el Clásico. El genial futbolista del Fenerbahçe ha tenido que pasar por el quirófano para superar unas molestias en la rodilla que no le impedían rendir al cien por cien. Una decisión compleja y valiente para llegar al tramo final de la temporada como un tiro. Ojalá una remontada como la de Isco, toda una lección de pundonor contra las lesiones. Afrontó el partido ante el PSG pensando en el Clásico. Tiene lógica si damos por sentado que ganar al Madrid significa atar media Liga, pero para los aficionados del Barça, el duelo ante los franceses sí que tenía trascendencia. Porque aunque los puntos no importaran tanto, había ganas de medir en qué escalón está su equipo. Un agente también debe saber cuándo guardar silencio. Recuperar las negociaciones con el Barça y explicar que Nico quería salir por ambición, señalando las limitaciones del Athletic, no le hace bien al jugador. Su expulsión en la Champions privó al Atlético de sumar tres puntos que se le presuponían y que puede terminar echando de menos para entrar en el top-8. No hay jornada sin polémica, sin club que no denuncie, sin entrenador que no se queje del árbitro o insinúe errores premeditados, sin declaración de Tebas... Demasiado ruido. En la zona media-baja de la Premier y con un pobre rendimiento en la Champions, el United sigue sin levantar cabeza. Y es una pena, porque es un gigante. El jaleo en el vestuario tras el 4-1 ante el Como es tremendo, pero se equivocan una y otra vez señalando al entrenador. Igual lo que está fallando, desde hace mucho tiempo, es el método y la planificación. El presidente de la Federación Griega de Baloncesto, un consejero de arbitraje, tres árbitros y un exjugador fueron detenidos tras una investigación por presuntos amaños de resultados y soborno en el baloncesto. Uno de los hechos que se conoce hasta el momento es el hallazgo de 820.000 euros en efectivo en el domicilio de un árbitro en una zona rural. Una trama que incluía hasta competiciones escolares. Otro episodio de corrupción lamentable.

articles.title: FIFA President Infantino’s re-election endorsed in U-turn by Asian football
articles.summary: Support crucial from 47-nation AFC’s president, who was critic of Gianni Infantino over failed private investment plan.
articles.body:
The head of the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) says the body is endorsing Gianni Infantino for another term as FIFA president.

The AFC has 47 member confederations. Even if all the members do not follow Friday’s direction from Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa, those that do could be key to guaranteeing another mandate for Infantino, who leads the governing body of world football and is seeking a fourth term.

The FIFA election is in March. The deadline for candidates to file against Infantino is November 18, and so far, none has filed.

Sheikh Salman, speaking at the AFC’s extraordinary congress in Tokyo on Friday, embraced Infantino with a large hug in front of the membership as he delivered his endorsement.

“We affirm our full commitment to supporting you and your leadership as you seek a new mandate as the FIFA president.” Sheikh Salman said.

“You’ve visited a lot of countries in Asia. I’ve spoken to a lot of members within this continent. I know your feeling, and I think your commitment is clear as well.”

Addressing his remarks to Infantino, Sheikh Salman indicated not every AFC member would go along with the endorsement but most will.

“My feeling is, I’m sure, the feeling of most of my members,” the AFC president said. “And I’ve said that to you.”

This is an abrupt turnaround for Sheikh Salman. Just over two months ago, the AFC joined the football governing bodies of Europe and that of North and Central America in saying Infantino had committed a “ fundamental breach of trust ”.

Infantino apologised last week in Zurich to FIFA’s 37-member ruling council, which he chairs, for “mistakes” he made in assembling a now-scrapped $4.2bn plan to sell a stake in FIFA events, including the World Cup, to private investors.

Sheikh Salman referenced the differences with Infantino in his speech but glossed over any details.

“Gianni, I want to make it clear: Yes, we had some issues we spoke about in the past,” Sheikh Salman said. “But let’s not relate the two things together. I think the last few days we met in Zurich, you made it clear that there’s a true understanding between us.”

“The past I’m sure is part of our history,” he added, “We’ve all, I’m sure, learned important lessons from it. What matters now is how we move forward together. I think everyone has questions, and I’m sure the answers will be available, whether to us in Asia or the rest of the world. ”

Infantino’s electioneering around the globe

FIFA’s media office has been promoting Infantino’s travels around the world, seeking votes in exchange for millions of more dollars in financial support for small and large football countries.

“Thank you for being here,” Sheikh Salman said to Infantino. “I know you have been everywhere. I don’t know how you can do it. But I’m sure that you set a record for being in almost every country.”

Sheikh Salman then joked that, perhaps, Infantino had a “clone”.

That drew a laugh. But the largest applause came at the end of his brief address when he again repeated his support for Infantino.

“As one Asian family, we are ready to move forward, united in your support, Gianni,” Sheikh Salman added. “I want to make that clear today.”

Infantino took the podium after Sheikh Salman and kept his remarks light. But he did acknowledge some errors.

“When you do many things, you do – hopefully, as we did, many good things – you do some mistakes as well,” Infantino said. “The important, however, is, as you said, to learn, to learn always from the experience, from the mistakes, to apologise, to move ahead, to come together, to unite, to build for our future, for your future.”

The largest applause came as he mentioned how, under his leadership, millions more are flowing to FIFA’s patronage network.

“Before I started as FIFA president, each of you – some of you are still [here] and still remember that time – each of you was receiving $1m every four years” Infantino said. “As of the first of January of next year, it will be $25m.”

articles.title: Pepe Brasín ve al Barcelonaa favorito en el Clásico: "El Madrid es un mar de dudas"
articles.standfirst: El periodista analizó en La Tribu, junto a Raúl Varela, las opciones de Real Madrid y Barcelona a 48 horas de un partido que puede marcar el rumbo de la Liga
articles.summary: El periodista analizó en La Tribu, junto a Raúl Varela, las opciones de Real Madrid y Barcelona a 48 horas de un partido que puede marcar el rumbo de la Liga
articles.body: Pepe Brasín tiene claro quién llega mejor al Clásico. En su conversación con Raúl Varela en La Tribu, el periodista destacó la mayor confianza del Barcelona frente a un Real Madrid que todavía busca soluciones en su juego. "El favoritismo del Barça tiene que ser altísimo", afirmó Brasín, que considera que el conjunto azulgrana transmite más seguridad en su modelo futbolístico. "El Barça tiene muchas más certezas, que el Madrid es como un yacimiento arqueológico", resumió, utilizando una metáfora para explicar el proceso de cambios que atraviesan los blancos. Brasín cree que el Real Madrid ha perdido un tiempo importante intentando mantener una fórmula que no estaba funcionando. "Los primeros dos meses de la temporada en los que trató de mantener el status quo (...) es obvio que eso no funciona", explicó durante el programa. Pese a ello, el periodista recordó que los blancos tienen argumentos suficientes para competir y ganar el partido. Para conseguirlo, considera fundamental la actuación de Kylian Mbappé. "para que el Madrid gane, tiene que ser un partido inmenso de Mbappé", señaló. En el bando azulgrana, Brasín destacó a Lamine Yamal como uno de los futbolistas capaces de marcar la diferencia en una cita de máxima exigencia. "A Lamine Yamal le encantan los grandes escenarios", apuntó. La posibilidad de que el Barcelona amplíe su ventaja hasta los nueve puntos añade presión al conjunto madridista. Brasín considera que esa circunstancia puede influir en el planteamiento y en la mentalidad de los jugadores. "El que tiene más que perder es el Madrid", afirmó. Además, advirtió de que el miedo a cometer errores podría condicionar a los blancos: "Posiblemente pueda hacer que el Madrid juegue más atenazado e incluso más conservador". Sin embargo, el periodista no descartó que el Real Madrid encuentre en el empate un resultado útil para mantener abierta la pelea por la Liga. "Creo que el empate es bueno para el Madrid", concluyó en su conversación con Varela.

articles.title: Wesley continues to draw interest in Premier League
articles.summary: Wesley is running, convincing, and attracting attention in the Premier League. The Brazilian winger is carving out an increasingly important role for himself...
articles.body:
Wesley is running, convincing, and attracting attention in the Premier League.

The Brazilian winger is carving out an increasingly important role for himself at Roma, as confirmed by his excellent performance against Slovan Bratislava.

His performances are not going unnoticed in England, where Manchester United and Arsenal are among the clubs interested in the player.

In recent weeks, Newcastle had also been linked with the Giallorossi full-back. However, that prospect appears to have cooled.

According to Football Insider , the Magpies have no intention of submitting an offer for the Brazilian, held back by two financial obstacles.

The first concerns the investments already made by the English club, which spent £29.5 million this summer to acquire a right-back. The second is linked to Roma's valuation, which is reportedly asking for between €50 and €60 million to let Wesley leave. Newcastle currently appears incapable of investing this sum.

Then there's the position of the Giallorossi, which has no intention of parting ways with the Brazilian in the January transfer window. This desire further complicates the plans of the English contenders and postpones any potential negotiations, at least for now.

articles.title: Bears’ Cairo Santos sounds off on rebounding from miss to sink Patriots with 58-yard bomb
articles.summary: Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson believes in Cairo Santos, and that is probably much easier to do because the longtime kicker strongly believes in himsel...
articles.body:
Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson believes in Cairo Santos , and that is probably much easier to do because the longtime kicker strongly believes in himself. Following a potentially costly miss that could have swayed momentum in the New England Patriots' favor, Santos quickly composed himself and fired a career-long 58-yard field goal that helped clinch a 30-24 win for his squad.

While mental fortitude is mandatory for this position, the 34-year-old Brazilian displayed impressive tenacity by making a milestone kick just minutes after committing a blunder.

"The misses annoy me, but like I can clear it so quick," Santos said, per Adam Jahns of CHGO Sports. "Like when (it's) the next opportunity, I just lock into my routine and I trust that I can execute."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Execute he did. The Tulane alum bounced the ball off the post on a 53-yard FG attempt with just over eight minutes left on the game clock. The miss enabled the Patriots to take over at their own 43-yard line and potentially capture the lead. Chicago's defense held strong, however, and forced a three-and-out. A brutal Caleb Williams sack then gave the kicker another opportunity to leave his mark on this Week 7 Thursday Night Football matchup.

Cairo Santos welcomed the chance for redemption, and for the first time in his 13-year NFL career, he connected on a 58-yarder. The Bears secured a 30-21 lead with 1:34 remaining, which meant the Patriots would need to complete a miraculous finish in order to snatch victory. They did not.

Santos' bomb proved to be the difference, and moreover, it showed just how resilient he can be when the pressure is approaching uncomfortable levels. The Bears (5-2) will vie for their third straight win when they face the Seattle Seahawks (3-3) in Week 8.

articles.title: Barcelona consider Sergio Busquets for future coaching role after Hansi Flick – report
articles.summary: Barcelona are keeping a close eye on Sergio Busquets’ development as a coach, with the former midfielder emerging as a potential candidate for an important r...
articles.body:
Barcelona are keeping a close eye on Sergio Busquets' development as a coach, with the former midfielder emerging as a potential candidate for an important role at the club.

Hansi Flick is currently leading the first team with some style, and his project very much seems to be in its early stages as things stand.

However, according to SPORT , Barcelona's sporting department views Busquets as someone with the potential to take on greater responsibilities in the future.

Busquets begins his coaching journey at Barcelona

The former Barcelona captain is currently gaining coaching experience with the club's reserve team, working alongside Juliano Belletti.

The arrangement allows Busquets to develop his understanding of coaching while remaining connected to the environment where he spent the majority of his playing career.

Sergio Busquets is learning the trade from Juliano Belletti. (Photo courtesy: FC Barcelona official website)

Barcelona believe his background and knowledge of the club could make him an interesting option for future responsibilities.

The club are also monitoring former midfielder Cesc Fabregas, whose impressive work at Como has placed him among the possible candidates to eventually succeed Flick.

However, neither candidate has been designated as the German coach's replacement, and it is too early to be having those conversations.

Why Busquets could be an interesting option for Barcelona

Few former players understand Barcelona's footballing identity as deeply as Busquets.

During his playing career, he was central to the team's positional structure, controlling possession, anticipating danger and helping team-mates find space.

His understanding of positioning and midfield organisation would be particularly valuable in a club that continues to place considerable importance on technical intelligence.

Barcelona are making plans for life after Hansi Flick. (Photo by Fran Santiago/Getty Images)

There is also precedent. In many ways, Busquets was a very similar player to Pep Guardiola and could look to follow the same path.

There is also an emotional dimension to the possibility of Busquets eventually taking on a prominent coaching role .

Having a former captain involved in shaping Barcelona's next generation is an idea that will always appeal to the football romantic.

Busquets still needs time to gain practical experience, develop his own methods and demonstrate his ability to manage players from the touchline.

It is still early days, but it is refreshing to see Barça already thinking about the future and how life after Hansi Flick might look.

While that scenario is unlikely to be anytime soon, the Catalan club are right to have a plan in place, and it remains to be seen how things pan out.

articles.title: Sunderland Reporter Notebook: No panic for Regis Le Bris' side despite sitting bottom of Premier League table
articles.summary: Why are Sunderland struggling in the Premier League after finishing seventh in their first season back in the top flight? Black Cats finding life tough balancing Europa League campaign and domestic ambitions with Brian Brobbey injury not aiding matters
articles.body:
This time around they sit bottom of the pile with four points from seven games. Things were always going to be tough with the additional load of European football to contend with, something Sunderland haven't experienced in over 50 years.

The performance at Bournemouth on Sunday, fresh from an away Europa league clash in Portugal, was littered with mistakes and individual errors.

It led to defender Nordi Mukiele suggesting post-match that the team had become "arrogant". That felt like the wrong choice of words from the Frenchman. I don't detect that mindset, but without doubt the schedule, both mentally and physically, is having an effect.

There was a feeling from within the club that those exertions of European football would be challenging this season, and that is playing out in the results.

The load has not been helped by concurrent injuries to strikers Brian Brobbey and Wilson Isidor early in the season, meaning the untested Timur Tutyerov has led the line in the last two games - which was not part of the plan at the start of the season.

Sunderland need to get back to basics and the things which made them so hard to beat last season. They only lost four games at the Stadium of Light across that entire campaign, making it something of a fortress.

It looked as though that would continue this season after a solid performance at home to champions Arsenal in September, off the back of a narrow win over Fulham. But the performance in the 2-0 loss to 10-man Brighton has sent alarm bells ringing.

I do fully expect them to rediscover those solid foundations on Wearside, with two home games in the next week against Leeds in the league and then Brentford in the Carabao Cup.

But to do that they need to get back to what they are good at - the snarling, physical, in-your-face, streetwise style that overpowered multiple teams last season.

Without that, they could find themselves in trouble.

Perhaps that is what Mukiele means - that they need to get the intensity and aggression back which served them so well last season. They have looked a bit timid at times this season, the complete opposite of their first season back in the Premier League.

In an ideal world, Sunderland wouldn't have been scrapping around on Deadline Day trying to sign players, but it was a frustrating window for sporting director Florent Ghisolfi. It took owner Kyril Louis Dreyfus to fly to Lyon personally and convince Malick Fofana to choose Sunderland over Crystal Palace with just hours of the window remaining.

They also had to make the Belgian winger a financial offer he couldn't refuse. But that was the conclusion to a summer which saw them struggle to get signings over the line, which was a source of confusion to many given the season they had just enjoyed - and the lure of European football.

In my opinion, the squad size is still decent and strong and they have two players for every position. But when big players aren't performing, and injuries to their potential replacements take hold, there is an obvious problem.

Regis Le Bris will be hoping he can call upon one of either Brobbey or Isidor against Leeds in what is already looking like a huge game on Sunday.

The season start has created a strange situation for fans, because Sunderland have begun their Europa League campaign well and the supporters are obviously enjoying that journey. But of course, they will be concerned by the sight of the Premier League table, though there was always an acceptance that this season would be difficult to balance and that the league form may take a hit as a result.

I spoke to a couple of Sunderland supporters in the summer who said a good season would be a run in Europe alongside survival in The Premier League. So I think the fanbase are honest enough to accept a drop off domestically, and won't be panicking yet.

They know with the likes of Granit Xhaka, Mukiele and Brobbey, they have an experienced spine which can help the team through these testing days.

The Sunderland fans have been through such a difficult time over the last decade that they won't be too phased by the current situation. But they will need to see an upturn in performances and results soon - starting at home to Leeds.

The only pressure I see on Le Bris at the moment will be that which he puts on himself. The 50-year-old has plenty credit in the bank after a couple of dream seasons on Wearside.

He has been a colossal part of everything good about Sunderland of late, and the club and fans will be backing him to turn things around. He is a very impressive operator, who leaves no stone unturned in his search for greatness and they are lucky to have him.

He also has a very solid support network around him at the Stadium of Light, and they are all on the same page. But he will be well aware things need to change domestically, and perhaps the comments from Mukiele post-match on Sunday will be the kick up the backside the Sunderland players need.

A word Le Bris uses often is "humble", and his players need to remind themselves what got them there in the first place. I'm confident they will be okay this season.

articles.title: Newcastle United Reporter Notebook: Matthias Jaissle needs some wins to quieten down the noise  on Tyneside
articles.summary: Newcastle have now lost three of their last four Premier League games to slip to 11th place in the Premier League, increasing the pressure on new boss Matthias Jaissle; watch Crystal Palace vs Newcastle United on Super Sunday on Sky Sports+ from 1230pm; kick-off 2pm
articles.body:
Matthias Jaissle's side have lost three of their last four Premier League games to slip to 11th place in the table and making Sunday's trip to Crystal Palace - live on Sky Sports - absolutely crucial.

What are the key issues and how does Jaissle fix them?

Newcastle are right at the bottom of the table when it comes to shots against and xG against and that must be a concern for the manager.

Yes, it's still early in the season and there is plenty of mitigation given how late he and his staff arrived in the summer, but unless that improves, it's going to be a very difficult season for the St James' Park club.

The 'vertical' style of football will work anywhere given time, the German claims, but the Premier League is punishing and Jaissle is having to learn as he goes. For me, he is trying to put square pegs into round holes to put a team together within his identity. But I'm not certain he has the players at his disposal to play the way he wants at this moment in time.

For example, Yoane Wissa has been used as a No 10 and in the last 10 minutes against Aston Villa last weekend even as a No 8. Joe Willock has also been deployed deeper as a 6 and new £51m signing Mathias Fernandez-Pardo has played largely as a No 9.

For me, all three of those are playing out of position and it has shown in performances. In recent games, Newcastle appear too easy to play through, the two-man midfield is overrun, and the defence are exposed. It's totally understandable that he wants to give his style a good go, but a more pragmatic approach may help stabilise things to get through the current choppy waters.

Jaissle hasn't been helped by an early-season injury crisis that has seen Dan Burn, Joelinton, Anthony Elanga, Amar Dedic, Tino Livramento and Jacob Ramsey, among others, all on the sidelines. But some of those players have now returned and he needs to work them back in while they are still getting up to speed.

The lengthy injury list was the last thing he needed when he was already chasing his tail after a turbulent summer. Newcastle are clearly missing the experience of Kieran Trippier, Bruno Guimaraes, Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon, and it is a much younger and inexperienced squad Jaissle has inherited from the one that finished last season under Eddie Howe.

It's the set up and it will take a while for the players to get used to Jaissle's ideas and plan. I think he needs to play an extra midfielder [Newcastle have the players for a 4-3-3 from the Howe tenure] to make the team a bit harder to beat.

The Geordie faithful were bewildered as to why Sean Steur [arguably their best player this season] and Aladji Bamba were left unused on the bench on Saturday, when Jaissle pushed Wissa back to a midfield role and threw Burn on up top.

An extra midfielder may give them a bit more control of games. As good a signing Nico Gonzalez is [£50m from Man City], the 23-year-old needs support in the engine room, and at times in recent games he has looked engulfed by opposition midfielders. You have to feel for him a bit.

Defenders Sven Botman and Malick Thiaw are coming in for criticism of late, but they have had very little protection from a threadbare midfield and have their work cut out.

The fact Newcastle conceded four to newly promoted Coventry, who had only scored one in their opening five Premier League games up until that point, tells its own story.

Steur has probably shown the most promise, but he has been used in fits and starts and Jaissle has mentioned his age [he's 18] a number of times when asked why he isn't starting. He looks like a top talent though and someone who doesn't hide when things are not going well. It was one of the reasons Newcastle signed him from a struggling Ajax team in the summer.

Amar Dedic also started the season on fire, but the injury he picked up last month has curtailed his progress and he is now battling to get his fitness back. I would expect him to come back into the starting lineup for the trip to Palace on Sunday.

Gonzalez I think will go on to be a good Newcastle player, but he needs support in midfield, and Fernandez-Pardo looks to be struggling with confidence. He has made it clear to the Newcastle hierarchy that he wants a chance to play as a central striker, but he looks like someone who would be more comfortable playing off the left of a 4-3-3, so they need to try and get the best out of that situation.

It's been a bit of a mixed bag for goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek so far, with a few top saves and a couple of costly mistakes, but there is great faith in him within the St James' Park recruitment team. Bazoumana Toure and Aladji Bamba have yet to start a Premier League match, and Newcastle need them to get up to speed quickly. They are not in a position where they can have £70m worth of players sat cooling their heels on the subs bench.

Yes, it's a transitional time on Tyneside, but Newcastle need players for now.

Is the new playing style and move to younger players showing any promise? And what's the mood of the fans?

It certainly looked like it was in the first matches of the season. The opening-day draw against Liverpool should have been a win and the follow-up visit to Tottenham was a win. Two excellent performances had the Newcastle fans singing the new manager's name.

But things have turned a bit in recent games and there were audible boos at full time on Saturday as Newcastle slipped to a rather tepid defeat to Villa. The visitors looked comfortable and controlled much of the game, so there were raised eyebrows within the media room when Jaissle said afterwards that his team had dominated.

Some supporters feel that Jaissle deserves the time to get his ideas across and it has always been the feeling from within the club that it may take time given the vast change we saw over the summer. Others though are worried about the future and think that the style of play is unsustainable.

Only time will tell. But despite the solid start to the season with those opening few performances, it feels like Jaissle needs a couple of wins to quieten down the noise in certain areas on Tyneside.

articles.title: Florian Wirtz is finally showing signs of life at Liverpool, but Andoni Iraola still needs more from his £116m playmaker
articles.summary: Florian Wirtz has contributed a goal or an assist in Liverpool's last three games, all wins, so can he now maintain that form as they prepare for a trio of huge games at Anfield? Watch Liverpool vs Brighton on Sunday on Sky Sports Premier League from 1230pm; kick-off 2pm
articles.body:
The headlines and chatter after Liverpool's 3-0 recent loss to Man City at Anfield, though, would not have made pretty reading for the club's £116m playmaker , with former Reds captain Jamie Carragher even going as far as suggesting the German needed to be axed from the team after another underwhelming showing against the Premier League leaders.

"I'm just sorry to say this Florian Wirtz signing it's not working and it hasn't worked so far and Gravenberch should not be sitting on the bench when Wirtz is playing for Liverpool" said the Sky Sports pundit. "It's not harsh to be having a go at Wirtz right now, he's got to do so much more.

"I struggle to think of one game where he's won Liverpool the game or he's been the man. He was brought in to be a star of the Premier League. I felt he could be the Kevin De Bruyne that at times got Man City over the line.

"Wirtz has been here for 55-60 games, it's a lot and I don't see it changing. Wirtz where he's almost nailed on that he plays every week in that No 10 position it has to stop.

"I think he needs to come out of the team, I said that last time out and I'm going to say it again."

But if seven days is a long time in politics, it is an eternity in football and Wirtz will head into the club's upcoming run of tricky fixtures with a spring in his step having shone in Liverpool's recent trio of wins at LASK and Brentford and home to Villarreal.

The 23-year-old pulled the strings in the visitors' 6-3 Champions League trouncing in Austria, creating the second of Bradley Barcola's hat-trick with a delightful inside pass in a tight space, before again producing the goods in west London to help the Reds came from behind and inflict Brentford's first defeat of the season on Saturday.

Iraola's side were still trailing the Bees' ten men when Wirtz's vision unlocked the home defence for Victor Munoz's well-taken leveller just past the hour mark, one of nine chances he created from open play in the contest - the most in a Premier League game since 2021 and the most in an away match for more than 15 years - while in total he has set up a league-high 20 openings this season.

And Wirtz then followed that up with a match-turning second-half cameo in Tuesday's 4-3 home win against Villarreal in which he scored his first goal since April - meaning he now has a goal involvement in three straight matches - as Liverpool made it five victories in their last six games in all competitions.

What is just as encouraging, though, as far as Iraola is concerned is the understanding Wirtz and his fellow £100m+ recruit from Paris Saint-Germain appeared to be developing on the lefthand side of the Reds' forward line in those victories as he looks to make his side more potent in attack.

"He's coming in from two very good games, he played very well LASK away, he helped the team a lot in possession, out of possession," was Iraola's assessment of Wirtz's last two performances.

"I hope we can keep him there. You ask me every day basically about him, we analyse and over scrutinise everything, but when he does well also, it's fair to say."

The Liverpool boss sounded exasperated he was still being quizzed about Wirtz and of course he would much prefer not to be, but when your big-money No 10 contributed just seven goals and ten assists in 49 games across all competitions in his debut campaign on Merseyside, then he has been in the game long enough to realise the outside noise will not simply go away after a few eye-catching showings.

For one thing, it is too small a sample size to start making definitive judgements on the Germany international, while the match conditions in both those encounters undoubtedly suited him coming against a LASK side making their Champions League debut and a Bees team forced to play the whole of the second half with only ten men following Yehor Yarmolyuk's straight red card.

The Ukrainian's needless dismissal in first-half stoppage time was undoubtedly a factor in allowing Wirtz to boss the second period at the Gtech as the hosts tired, allowing the playmaker more space and time in which to operate and so create most of those nine chances.

However, a deeper dive into the stats show that of those nine openings, six came after Brentford went down to ten men, while none were actually classified as 'big chances' by Opta as the Reds largely struggled to break down the home side, symptomatic really of the team's attacking struggles as a whole, where they rank only 16th for xG in the Premier League so far this season.

And it is a similar story with those Premier-League high 20 openings Wirtz has created this campaign, with again none being deemed high-quality by Opta.

This is the catch 22 for Iraola as he prepares for potentially season-defining games at Anfield against high-flying Brighton & Hove Albion and champions Arsenal in the league - where Liverpool have not won since April 25 and have just 11 victories there in their last 21 games in total - separated by a League Cup clash with free-scoring Chelsea, over the course of the next 10 days.

On the one hand, the Basque will be desperate for Wirtz to keep performing in these trio of high-octane clashes - all live on Sky Sports - that are likely to be tight affairs in which your big-money playmaker is hoped to make the difference.

But on the other hand, can he risk playing the No 10 against opponents with players who can really hurt the Reds on the counter, as we saw at St James' Park on the opening weekend of the season, when Newcastle United twice punished Liverpool with fast breaks through the middle? And can he actually count on him to show up in matches where he will have less time on the ball and space with which to make those decisive passes?

This was, of course, the very dilemma Iraola's predecessor had following Wirtz's arrival at the start of last season when Arne Slot changed the makeup of his title-winning midfield to accommodate the German in the 'hole', with disastrous consequences, before reverting back to the previous campaign's successful 4-3-3 diamond formation with Gravenberch as a sole No 6 and shunting the new man out to the left.

Iraola never played with 'specialist' No 6s in front of his back four at Bournemouth, though, instead trusting Tyler Adams and Alex Scott to get up and down the pitch and has so far resisted employing Gravenberch as a holding midfielder, meaning he is unlikely to follow suit.

But finding that midfield balance is integral to the success, or otherwise, of Wirtz's Reds career, as Sky Sports News' Liverpool reporter Vinny O'Connor told the latest Sky Sports Premier League podcast:

"If it's not working then he'll [Iraola] take a big decision [to drop Wirtz] and make that call ultimately. It is to do with the players around him and it is finding that balance in midfield and he's not necessarily helped I don't think by the fact that Liverpool don't have an out-and-out destroyer who can sit in front of that back four.

"At the moment, Gravenberch has played that role, but we've seen again at times this season how he wants to drive forward as well and play a part higher up the pitch. MacAllister, obviously that suits him better and [Dominik] Szoboszlai isn't someone who naturally sits and holds in midfield either.

"So there's a dynamic in that midfield - who does what and when and when you've got Wirtz in there, that leaves Liverpool at times completely wide open. We've seen how they've been caught on the counterattack, so solving that problem is going to be key to getting the best out of Wirtz

"At the moment, you've got that solidity behind him and at times Wirtz has played even further forward than a No 10, almost as like a second striker off [Alexander] Isak and if their relationship thrives and you've got the pace on the wings from the likes of Barcola and the threat that he provides as well occupying defenders, maybe that opens up more spaces for Wirtz, gives him more time on the ball, more time to be creative and ultimately make the kind of impact that we're expecting from him."

Playing in a team that is regularly winning and bossing games will undoubtedly massively help Wirtz going forward, something he has not had the luxury of much since joining the club and Iraola will hope that is the now case in these huge games coming up.
